identity.title: Standard Air Contaminant Discharge Permit
identity.issuer: State of Oregon Department of Environmental Quality, Northwest Region

scan.summary: This is an Oregon DEQ air permit authorizing Cascade Specialty Chemicals to operate chemical storage and repackaging equipment with vapor control at its Portland facility. The permit specifies which air contaminant sources are allowed, how they must be operated and monitored, what records must be kept, and what happens if conditions are violated. Meeting the permit's conditions is the company's obligation; the permit itself is the agency's document and contains no gaps to fix.
scan.freshness_note: This permit expires November 15, 2026—52 days from today (September 25, 2026). Renewal application was due July 18, 2026, which has already passed. This is now overdue and a critical compliance failure if not already submitted.

expected_missing.title: Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plan (SWPPP) or Industrial Stormwater Permit
expected_missing.why: Chemical storage and handling at a facility in Portland (near the Columbia River) typically requires stormwater management to prevent contamination runoff.

expected_missing.title: Spill Prevention, Control and Countermeasure (SPCC) Plan
expected_missing.why: Storage of 40,000 gallons of solvents (4 tanks × 10,000 gallons) in or near navigable waters triggers EPA SPCC requirements.

expected_missing.title: Right-to-Know (Tier II) chemical inventory reports
expected_missing.why: Chemical storage operations above certain thresholds must file EPCRA Section 312 Tier II reports with local fire departments and emergency agencies.

scan.confidence_notes: High confidence on all permit details. The document is a standard Oregon DEQ air permit clearly written and unambiguous on face. However, there is a **critical compliance alert**: the renewal application deadline of July 18, 2026, has already passed as of today (September 25, 2026). If the renewal application was not submitted by that date, the company is now in violation. Section 1.3 states that a timely and complete renewal application allows continued operation until the Department acts, but the failure to file by July 18 is itself a violation unless the company can show a timely filing. The permit itself expires November 15, 2026 (52 days away). The company should immediately contact Oregon DEQ Northwest Region to determine the status of its renewal application and whether a late application can still be accepted. If no renewal application was filed, operations should cease on November 15, 2026, or the company risks enforcement action. The document provides no information about the company's actual compliance record with daily monitoring, quarterly inspections, annual reporting, or excess emission notifications, so the company's operational compliance cannot be assessed from the permit alone.
